# mikado

mikado keeps a goal visible while the work behind it grows. A **quest** is a goal crowned by one
deed, its **crowning deed**; the deeds it requires, and the deeds those require, form a **chart**
from today's work to the goal. You record what you unearth as you go; the dashboard draws the
chart as a skill tree.

You talk to mikado through its CLI. Every command except `serve` and `skill` is a client of a
local server.

## Before anything

- Run `mikado quest list`. If it fails with "connection refused", the server is not running:
  tell the user to start it with `mikado serve` (it is their long-running process — do not
  start or stop it yourself).
- `mikado help` is the full command reference. Add `--json` to any read command to get
  machine-readable output; prefer it when you need to act on the result (see
  [JSON field names](#json-field-names)).

## The model

- **Deed** (also called a **task** — the two words mean the same): one unit of work on the
  chart. Three kinds:
  - **issue** — a GitHub issue (`owner/repo#n`). Its title, state and assignees come live from
    GitHub. It is *fulfilled* when the issue is closed; closed as "not planned" or "duplicate"
    it reads as *abandoned*. You never mark an issue fulfilled in mikado — close it on GitHub.
  - **errand** — a real step not worth an issue ("book the store-page feature slot").
  - **petition** — something we await a reply on from someone, often outside the team
    ("final key art from the freelance artist").
- **Requires / opens**: "M5 requires M3" means M3 must be fulfilled before M5; said the other
  way round, M3 opens M5. The only blocking link. Cycles are refused.
- **Quest**: a slug (e.g. `winter-update`), a title and a crowning deed. Its deeds are *computed*:
  the crowning deed, everything it requires (transitively) — the **main quest** — and their
  side quests. A deed joins a quest by being linked in; it leaves when the link is cut.
- **Side quest**: optional polish hung on a deed (`--side-of`). Never blocks anything; earns an
  achievement, not progress.
- **Status** (computed): *fulfilled*, *open* (everything it requires is fulfilled), *sealed*
  (something it requires is not), *awaiting reply* (an open petition), *abandoned* (won't do:
  stays on the chart, blocks nothing, counts in no total).
- **Underway** is separate from status: `mikado take-up D` means someone is on it right now;
  `mikado set-down D` means they stopped.
- **Hero**: who is responsible for a deed — its GitHub assignee, else the hero set in mikado.

## Ids — use them exactly

- A **deed** has one global id, `M` plus a number: `M142`. The same deed has the same id in
  every quest. Commands also accept `M-142`, `m142`, `142`, `owner/repo#n` or an issue URL.
- A **quest** is named by its slug: `winter-update`.
- When you report back to the user, name deeds by their `M` id (and the issue ref if it helps):
  "Added M12 (studio/saves#45); it opens M9."

## Workflows

**Start a quest.** Create it, then its crowning deed.

    mikado quest new "The winter update ships to every player"   # prints the slug
    mikado add studio/game#140 --crowns winter-update-ships-every

**Chart what the goal requires.** Link each prerequisite to the deed it opens.

    mikado add studio/saves#88 --opens M1
    mikado errand "Book the store-page feature slot with the platform" --opens M1 --hero ada

**You unearthed something while working on a deed** — the most important habit. Always say
where it was found and why; that is how the quest's chronicle stays readable.

    mikado add studio/saves#91 --opens M3 --unearthed-on M3 --reason "old saves crash the loader"
    mikado petition "Final key art from the freelance artist" --on "freelance artist" \
        --opens M5 --unearthed-on M5 --reason "placeholder art only; the stores reject it"

**Optional polish** goes in a side quest, not in the requirements:

    mikado errand "Snowfall particles on the title screen" --side-of M2

**The same issue serves another quest.** Add it again with a link — you get the existing deed
back, now in both quests:

    mikado add studio/saves#88 --opens M40

**Progress.**

    mikado take-up M7 --by dex    # someone is on it now (underway)
    mikado fulfil M7                # errands and petitions only; issues close on GitHub
    mikado set-down M7              # stopped without fulfilling it

**Something will not happen.** Abandon it — it stays visible, stops blocking, and its side
quests are abandoned with it. Strike only what should never have been there.

    mikado abandon M10 --reason "split-screen co-op is cut from this update"
    mikado strike M11 --reason "added to the wrong quest by mistake"

**Look before you change.**

    mikado quest show winter-update      # the chart: deeds, status, requirements, chronicle
    mikado show M3                       # one deed: what it requires, what it opens, its quests
    mikado quest show winter-update --json # the same, for you to parse

**Show the user.** `mikado open` opens the dashboard in their browser: the Quest Board, a
quest's chart, or the chart with one deed selected. `--print` gives just the URL, to paste into
a reply.

    mikado open winter-update
    mikado open M9 --print

## Commands and flags

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `quest new "title" [--crown D]` | start a quest |
| `quest crown SLUG D` | make D the quest's crowning deed |
| `add owner/repo#n` / `errand "title"` / `petition "title" --on WHO` | add a deed |
| `require D PREREQ` / `unrequire D PREREQ` | D requires PREREQ / no longer |
| `fulfil D` / `unfulfil D` | errands and petitions only |
| `take-up D [--by WHO]` / `set-down D` | underway / no longer |
| `abandon D --reason` / `unabandon D` | won't do / undo that |
| `strike D --reason` | gone for good, stays only in the chronicle |
| `set D --hero WHO` | set the hero (`-` for no hero) |

Link flags on `add`, `errand` and `petition`: `--opens D` (D requires the new deed),
`--requires D`, `--side-of D`, `--crowns SLUG`, `--unearthed-on D --reason "why"`, `--hero WHO`,
`--npc`. Earlier names (`done`, `cancel`, `remove`, `start`, `need`, `await`, `quest final`,
`--needed-by`, `--needs`, `--found-while`, `--final-of`, `--owner`, `--final`) still work, but
use the ones above.

## JSON field names

`--json` output and the API keep plain, older names. Read them as:

| In JSON | Means |
|---|---|
| `status: "done"` | Fulfilled |
| `status: "available"` | Open |
| `status: "locked"` (with `openBefore`: how many to go) | Sealed |
| `status: "awaiting"` | Awaiting reply |
| `status: "cancelled"`, `cancelled`, `cancelReason` | Abandoned, and why |
| quest `state: "complete"` / `"cancelled"` | quest fulfilled / abandoned |
| quest `archivedAt` | archived (absent when not) |
| `kind: "awaiting"`, `waitingOn`, `since` | a Petition, whom it awaits, since when |
| `final`, `finalCardId`, `finalOf` | the crowning deed |
| `needs` (`from` requires `to`), `neededBy` | Requires, Opens |
| `sideOf` | a side quest on that deed |
| `foundWhile`, `reason` | unearthed while on that deed, and why |
| `working`, `workingBy`, `workingSince` | underway |
| `owner`, `assignees` | the hero (GitHub assignees first) |
| `log` | the chronicle |
| `id` / `key` | the deed (`key` is `M142`) |

## Glossary

The words mikado uses, everywhere a person or an agent reads them.

| # | Word | Meaning | CLI |
|---|---|---|---|
| G1 | Quest | A goal: small enough to finish, big enough to need several deeds. It is drawn as a chart that ends in one crowning deed. | `quest new "title"` |
| G2 | Quest Board | The page with every quest at a glance: progress on its main quest, its achievements, and who is on it. | `quest list`, `open` |
| G3 | Chart | One quest drawn out: every deed on the way to the crowning deed, and what requires what. | `quest show SLUG`, `open SLUG` |
| G4 | Deed (or Task) | Any unit on the chart, named by its id, like M142. "Task" means exactly the same; either word works. | `show D` |
| G5 | Issue | A deed that is a GitHub issue (owner/repo#n). Its title, state and assignees come from GitHub; it is fulfilled when the issue is closed. | `add owner/repo#n` |
| G6 | Errand | A deed that is a real step but not worth a GitHub issue, like booking a release window. | `errand "title"` |
| G7 | Petition | A deed that waits on someone, often outside the team, like a production token from a vendor. It says whom it awaits a reply from, and since when. | `petition "title" --on WHO` |
| G8 | Crowning deed | The one deed whose fulfilment fulfils the quest. Everything else on the main quest leads to it. | `quest crown SLUG D`, `--crowns SLUG` |
| G9 | Main quest | The required path: the crowning deed and every deed it requires, directly or not. Its progress is the quest's progress. | |
| G10 | Side quest | Optional polish hung on a deed. It never blocks anything and counts as an achievement, not as progress. | `--side-of D` |
| G11 | Achievement | What a fulfilled side quest earns: a star beside the quest's progress, never a requirement. | |
| G12 | Requires / Opens | The only blocking link. "M5 requires M3" means M3 must be fulfilled first; said the other way round, M3 opens M5. Cycles are refused. | `require D PREREQ`, `--requires D`, `--opens D` |
| G13 | Unearthed | A deed found while working on another, recorded with where and why: "unearthed while on M3: old saves crash the loader". | `--unearthed-on D --reason "why"` |
| G14 | Fulfilled | Status: finished. An issue is fulfilled when it closes on GitHub; an errand or a petition when it is marked so. | `fulfil D` |
| G15 | Open | Status: everything it requires is fulfilled (or abandoned), so it can be started now. | |
| G16 | Sealed | Status: blocked. Something it requires is not fulfilled yet; the badge counts what is left, as in "sealed · 2 to go". | |
| G17 | Awaiting reply | Status of a petition that is otherwise open: only the person it waits on stands in the way. | |
| G18 | Abandoned | Status: won't be done. It stays on the chart, blocks nothing and counts in no total; its side quests are abandoned with it. An issue closed on GitHub as not planned or duplicate reads as abandoned. | `abandon D --reason "why"`, `unabandon D` |
| G19 | Struck | Gone for good: taken off the chart with its side quests, and kept only in the chronicle. Prefer abandoning. | `strike D --reason "why"` |
| G20 | Underway | Someone is on it right now, apart from its status. You take a deed up when you start and set it down when you stop. | `take-up D [--by WHO]`, `set-down D` |
| G21 | Hero / no hero | Whoever is responsible for a deed: its GitHub assignee, else the hero set in mikado. A deed with neither shows "no hero". | `--hero WHO`, `set D --hero WHO` |
| G22 | Chronicle | The history: every change as one sentence. A quest's chronicle is its own events plus those of the deeds on its chart. | `quest show SLUG` |
| G23 | NPC | A decorative joke badge any deed can wear. Nothing reads it. | `--npc` |
| G24 | Archived | A quest put away: off the Quest Board's shelves and out of `quest list` (unless `--all`), its chart, deeds and chronicle untouched. Archive a quest only when the user asks. | `quest archive SLUG`, `quest unarchive SLUG` |

## Rules

- Record what you unearth with `--unearthed-on` and `--reason`. Never add an unearthed deed
  silently.
- Prefer `abandon` over `strike`. Striking erases a deed from every quest it serves.
- Do not assign or unassign people on GitHub (`mikado assign`) unless the user asked: it changes
  the issue for everyone. Setting a hero on GitHub is the user's call.
- Do not create GitHub issues on your own to put them in a quest. If a step is worth an issue,
  ask; otherwise use an errand.
- A deed added with no link is in no quest; mikado warns. Link it (`--opens`, `--side-of`,
  `mikado require`) or say why not.
- If a command fails, report mikado's message as it is — it names the deed and the reason
  (for example the cycle a `require` would create).
- Do not start or stop the mikado server; it is the user's.
